steps.title: Versatile
steps.body: Pinot Noir's low tannin and high acidity make it one of the most food-friendly reds. It suits roast chicken, duck, salmon, tuna, mushrooms and game birds. Burgundy matches boeuf bourguignon and coq au vin. Its low tannin even works with some fish.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 14 to 16 degrees, slightly cooler than big reds, in a large bowl glass. Simple Pinot is best within five years. Top Burgundy ages 10 to 30 years, developing mushroom, truffle, game and forest floor. Decanting isn't always needed; it can lose delicate aromas.

steps.prompt: Why does Pinot Noir pair well with salmon?
options: Its low tannin doesn't clash with fish
steps.explanation: High tannin can make fish taste metallic; Pinot's low tannin avoids that.

steps.body: Mushroom risotto with an older Pinot Noir is a near-perfect match. The earthy notes in both bring each other forward.

steps.explanation: Very hot curry clashes with most reds.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Noir suits duck, salmon and mushrooms
Serve at 14 to 16 degrees in a large glass
